get.summary: A page of customers, ready to render
get.description:
Every row includes all searchable customer, service-account, location and equipment values, so the client never performs follow-up lookups.

With `q`, the same response shape is ranked by fuzzy relevance and includes `matchedFields` and `score`.

`q` performs ranked fuzzy search across customer identity, account numbers, addresses, location paths/codes and service equipment identifiers.

Paging is by `cursor`, not page number: pass back `nextCursor` until it is null. At 300k rows a page-50000 offset costs 89ms and keyset costs 0.03ms, and a cursor cannot skip or repeat rows when someone inserts while you scroll. `total` comes back on the first page only.

post.summary: Register a subscriber, optionally with their first connection
post.description:
The subscriber code is minted by the database, not sent in: two collectors registering at two doors in the same minute must not be handed the same one. The first connection takes that code as its service account number, and later lines suffix off it (`SSCN-0042-A1`).

The customer and the connection land in one transaction. A customer with no line is reachable only by a tenant-wide account, because every area-scoped screen finds customers through where their lines are fitted — so an area-scoped caller must send `connection`, and its `locationId` must sit inside the areas they cover.

The response is the same shape as `GET /customers/:id`, so the client renders the new subscriber without a follow-up call.

get.summary: Everything a customer details page draws, in one response
get.description:
A customer id is a handle onto a graph — subscriptions, and through each one a provider, a package, a service and a location.

This resolves the whole graph server-side, where the joins are indexed, so the client makes no follow-up calls to `/packages/:id`, `/service-providers/:id` or `/locations/:id`.

Out of your area answers 404 rather than 403: whether a customer exists elsewhere is not something the caller should learn.

patch.summary: Move a connection onto a different package
patch.description:
The package must belong to the same provider as the line: crossing providers would orphan the service account number, which is a new connection rather than a plan change.

Nothing is prorated. `outstanding_balance` is only ever written down by a payment — no job accrues the monthly fee — so there is no part-cycle to split. The new price is what the next charge will use.

`price` overrides the package list price for this one customer. Omitted, the line takes the package price.

post.summary: Add another package to a customer as its own line — an addon, or a second connection
post.description:
An addon is a subscription of its own rather than a flag on an existing one, because that is the shape the data has: one package per line, one balance per line. It therefore bills, collects and appears on every screen that already reads lines.

`basedOn` names the line it sits beside. The provider, installation location and address are inherited from it, so an addon cannot be created somewhere the base connection is not. The new line gets its own account number, suffixed off the base: `SSCN-0042-A1`.

It starts at a zero balance. Money is taken through `POST /payments/subscription` against the new line like any other.

post.summary: Upload a file
post.description: A `multipart/form-data` body with one `file` part. Identical bytes already stored are reused rather than uploaded twice — the response says so with `deduplicated`. The signed `url` it returns is what a notification `imageUrl` expects.

id.description: The user-file id — what every other endpoint takes

deduplicated.description: True when these exact bytes were already stored

get.summary: A fresh signed download URL for one file

expiresAt.description: Null for a public file — its URL is durable and does not expire.

delete.description: Soft delete. The stored object is removed later by the storage cleanup job, once nothing else references those bytes.

get.summary: The people this operator employs
get.description:
Every row carries the areas the person reaches, split into the grants held on them (`locations`) and the ones inherited from their crew (`inheritedLocations`) — so a screen can show why someone reaches an area without a second call.

`locationId` asks the operational question instead: who serves this address? A grant on the node or on any ancestor of it counts, because a grant covers its whole subtree.

Scoped like every other list: `ALL` returns the tenant, `LOCATION` returns the staff working inside your areas, `TEAM` returns your own crew.

post.summary: Hire someone, or give an existing account a job here
post.description:
An `email` or a `phone` is required — one of them is how the person signs in.

The account is found before it is created: somebody who already signs in as another operator’s subscriber gets a second membership, not a second login. `password` is therefore rejected when the account already exists; those people set their own.

`locationIds` grants areas in the same call. You can only grant areas you hold yourself, and only a tenant-wide grant may appoint an `admin`.

get.summary: The UPI handles this tenant collects into
get.description:
Ordered with the default first, then oldest — the order a picker should show them in.

Live handles only unless `includeInactive` is set, which needs nothing extra: an inactive handle is one the office stood down, and its QR at a door would send money nowhere anybody is watching.

post.summary: Add a UPI handle
post.description: The first handle added is the default whatever the body says — a list of one with nothing marked leaves the collector no QR to show.

patch.summary: Edit a UPI handle, or make it the default
patch.description: Standing the only live handle down is refused: it would empty the collector's picker.

delete.description: Removing the default passes it to the oldest surviving handle, rather than leaving the tenant with handles but none chosen.

get.summary: Complaints this caller may see
get.description:
Scoped by the grant on `tickets.view`. At ALL it is the whole tenant; at LOCATION it is the areas the caller covers plus anything they raised or hold; at ASSIGNED or TEAM it is their own, their team's, and anything still unclaimed in their areas — an unassigned fault nobody can see is a fault nobody fixes; at OWN it is only what they raised or hold.

`openOnly` folds together every status a ticket is still worked on in, which is what an operator means by "open".

`assignedTo=me` resolves to the caller, so a handset does not need its own user id.

post.summary: Raise a complaint against a customer or one of their lines
post.description:
The ticket number is minted by the database off the tenant's own counter — `SSCN-T-000042` — so it reads as a family with the subscriber code and two people raising one in the same second cannot collide.

The area is copied from the named line, or from the customer's first line when none is named. That is what every area-scoped list filters on, so a customer with no connection at all produces a ticket only a tenant-wide account will see.

Passing `assignedTo` needs `tickets.assign` as well.

get.summary: One complaint, with the customer and line it is about
get.description: Out of the caller's reach answers 404 rather than 403: whether a ticket exists elsewhere is not something the caller should learn.

patch.summary: Change a complaint — its status, priority, category or notes
patch.description:
Moving one to `resolved`, `closed` or `cancelled` needs `tickets.resolve` on top of `tickets.update`: reprioritising is field work, but telling a subscriber their fault is fixed is not.

`resolved` requires a resolution, because that text is what the customer is told. `resolvedAt` is stamped once, when the ticket first settles, and a later edit never moves it.

post.summary: Hand a complaint to somebody, or put it back in the pool
post.description: Assigning an `open` ticket also moves it to `in_progress` — handing it over is the moment it stops being a queue entry. `assignedTo: null` releases it.
